name: v1.1.0 — Demo Experience & Conversation Archiving
body:
## Agentic Customer Support System v1.1.0

This release updates the demo experience and adds tools for reviewing archived conversations, while preserving the existing Gemini, Cloud Run, Cloudflare Workers, PostgreSQL, Redis, LangGraph, and Opik setup.

### What's new
- Redesigned landing page and matching chat theme, with desktop/mobile layouts, an interactive illustrative agent trace, architecture diagrams, and clearly labelled evaluation and benchmark evidence.
- Cloudflare Workers preview configuration and documentation for connecting previews to a separate staging API.
- Conversation archiving before retention cleanup, including messages, events, refund context, token usage, and trace IDs. Archived transcripts are retained for 90 days by default.
- Breach checks and a read-only triage CLI for listing, inspecting, scanning, and exporting demo conversations into candidate evaluation cases.
- Safer retention handling with transactional archive-before-delete behavior, concurrent cleanup protection, and improved dry-run reporting.
- Refreshed README, deployment instructions, and conversation-triage documentation.

### Validation and deployment
- All 11 CI jobs passed on the release commit.
- Backend: 130 tests passed and 1 skipped in each of the SQLite and PostgreSQL/Redis runs.
- PostgreSQL and SQLite migration upgrade/downgrade/upgrade checks passed.
- Frontend and landing builds, Cloudflare configuration dry run, desktop/mobile browser checks, container smoke checks, and load smoke checks passed.
- All 76 scripted evaluation cases passed; 7 live-only cases were skipped.
- Cloud Run migration and rollout, Cloudflare Workers production build, and GitHub Pages deployment succeeded. The production readiness check confirmed PostgreSQL and Redis connectivity.

### Known limitations
- Live Gemini evaluations were not run because the GitHub Actions Gemini secret is unavailable. The deployed API retains its existing Gemini configuration.
- Existing high- and moderate-severity frontend/landing dependency advisories remain unresolved.
- Breach checks are review aids and do not detect every possible attack.
